findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm that `etc.` in P11 uses a pattern that actually matches (e.g., `\betc\.` with no trailing `\b`, or `(?<![\w])etc\.(?![\w])`) rather than `\betc\.\b`, which can never match since `\.` is a non-word char and `\b` after it requires a word char to follow.
evidence: 'both word boundaries' applied to `etc.` → \betc\.\b; \b after \.  requires the next char to be \w, but `etc.` is followed by non-word chars in all realistic AC text
The plan explicitly states '`etc.` kept' and the Testing section enumerates 'etc.' in positive-fire cases ('handles errors, etc.'), making this a directly-tested requirement that would silently fail
findings.finding: The plan says the fixed P11 lexicon uses 'both word boundaries' for all terms, but applying a trailing \b to `etc.` produces the pattern \betc\.\b, which can never match because \b after a literal dot (a non-word char) requires the immediately following character to be a word character — whereas `etc.` is always followed by whitespace, comma, or EOL. This would silently drop `etc.` from P11 detection entirely, breaking the one term the plan explicitly says is KEPT.
findings.location: Approach section — 'fixed lexicon (both word boundaries; `clean` dropped; `etc.` kept)'
scenarios: AC item 'handles errors, etc. gracefully' — P11 fires on 'etc.' as intended per plan — but \betc\.\b never matches, so the positive test case silently passes instead of firing
The plan's own enumerated positive case ('handles errors, etc. with no adjacent code span') fails to block
findings.suggested_fix: For `etc.` specifically, use `re.search(r'\betc\.', line)` (leading boundary only, since the literal dot already anchors the right side) or wrap it in a negative lookahead: `re.search(r'(?<!\w)etc\.(?!\w)', line)`. Other purely alphabetic terms in the lexicon can safely use `\bterm\b`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify the multi-span disambiguation rule for the `etc.` proximity exemption: specify whether the check uses the nearest preceding span's end, the last span's end before `etc.`, or any span on the line — and add a multi-span fixture case to the enumerated FP set.
evidence: 'a recorded span's end' — singular indefinite article does not resolve ambiguity for multi-span lines
Fixture line: 'run `git grep -n \'pattern\' docs/ src/`, etc.' — one span, but the general rule must handle N spans
findings.finding: The `etc.` span-proximity exemption is defined as 'an `etc.` occurrence whose start lies within 30 characters after A RECORDED SPAN'S END' (singular). The plan does not specify behavior when multiple code spans appear on the same line before `etc.` — whether to use the nearest preceding span's end, the last span's end, or any span on the line. The Testing fixture line 'run `git grep -n \'pattern\' docs/ src/`, etc.' has the span ending roughly 8 chars before `etc.`, which likely falls within 30, but the disambiguation rule still needs to be stated for correctness in multi-span edge cases.
findings.location: Approach section — 'an `etc.` occurrence whose start lies within 30 characters after a recorded span's end is exempt'
scenarios: AC item with two code spans followed by `etc.`: '`pytest` and `make check`, etc.' — should be exempt, but if the rule only checks the FIRST span's end (not the nearest/last), the 30-char window may expire and `etc.` incorrectly fires
findings.suggested_fix: Use the nearest preceding span's end (i.e., the span whose end position is the largest value still less than the `etc.` start position) — this is the most natural 'trailing enumeration' reading and is straightforward to implement with `max(end for start, end in spans if end < etc_start, default=-999)`.

findings.suggested_fix: Add tests/unit/plan_review/test_det_citation.py to the Scope edit list. In that test, construct the PlanContext description so no vague lexicon terms appear, ensuring the result stays non-blocking (verifying only the citation-gap advisory lane). Alternatively, split the assertion: r.blocking is False when the vague lexicon does not fire.

findings.finding: Promoting any finding from `p6_ac_quality` (R2 vague-lexicon fix) or adding a new blocking R1 check that flows through P6 requires updating files outside `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` that explicitly assert P6 / `p6_ac_quality` is advisory and 'never blocks'. These consumers are not enumerated in the Scope. Specifically: `tests/unit/test_det_floor_operator_attested.py` (module docstring line 4: 'it is ADVISORY (never blocks)'), `tests/unit/plan_review/test_det_citation.py` (module docstring line 5 and comment line 92), and `docs/plan-review-gate.md` (line 90: 'P4/P6/P7 … are advisory'; line 103: 'It NEVER blocks (it rides P6, which is advisory)').
findings.location: Approach section / Scope section — unenumerated consumers

findings.finding: The R1 trigger condition 'verification phrase' is not enumerated anywhere in the plan, leaving the implementing agent to choose which phrases qualify with no specification to validate against. Different phrase sets produce materially different backtest outcomes.
findings.location: Approach section: 'a backtick command, test reference, or verification phrase'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence such as: 'Verification phrases: any of `assert`, `verify`, `check`, `confirms`, `ensure` (case-insensitive word-boundary match).' Tie the phrase list explicitly to the backtest corpus.

findings.finding: The 16 backtest AC fixtures used in AC3 are not specified or pointed to, so an implementing agent cannot deterministically reproduce the parameterized test that is supposed to prove zero false-positives on the exact corpus cases.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'The fixed lexicon produces zero matches on the 16 previously false-positive AC fixtures taken from the backtest (checked: parameterized test reproducing those AC lines).'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scope entry such as `tests/unit/fixtures/p6_fp_backtest.py` containing the 16 AC strings verbatim, and reference it from AC3.

findings.finding: The `etc.` code-span proximity exemption measures distance ambiguously: after stripping inline code spans the code span no longer exists in the text, making 'within 30 chars of a code span' unmeasurable on the stripped string.
findings.location: Approach section, R2: 'keep `etc.` with a code-span-proximity exemption (within 30 chars)'
findings.suggested_fix: Measure `etc.` proximity on the ORIGINAL line before stripping: record all `[start, end]` code-span positions via a first-pass regex scan, then check whether any `etc.` occurrence falls within 30 chars of a span boundary; only then strip and match the remaining vague terms.

findings.finding: The R1 check's scope on container tickets is unspecified — the plan says 'leaf plan' but does not state what R1 does when `ctx.has_children` is True.
findings.location: Approach section, R1: 'a leaf plan must have >= 1 `- [ ]` AC item'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach section: 'R1 is a leaf-only check; when `ctx.has_children` is True, R1 returns a pass (mirroring the P5 container-guard pattern).'
